title: app-shell: a backgrounded tab polls approvals + inbox every 60 s forever, so a forgotten tab keeps scale-to-zero servers (staging) awake 24/7: stop polling after N minutes hidden
body:
## Problem

A tab left open on a console page never lets its server go idle. `packages/app-shell/src/hooks/sharedUserFeeds.ts` keeps polling while the tab is hidden: `HIDDEN_POLL_MS = 60_000` against `APPROVALS_POLL_MS = 30_000` / `INBOX_POLL_MS = 10_000` in the foreground. So a backgrounded tab still sends `GET /api/v1/approvals/requests` and `GET /api/v1/data/sys_inbox_message` every 60 s, forever.

That matters wherever the backend scales to zero. Since cloud#2766 (2026-10-12), the staging runtime and control-plane containers sleep after 15 / 30 idle minutes, and a 60 s poll is always inside that window. Measured with Cloudflare HTTP analytics:

| window (UTC) | host | approvals/requests | sys_inbox_message | cadence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10-13 15:00–20:00 | `cloud.objectos.app` (staging console) | 607 | 588 | ~30 s, foreground |
| 10-14 12:00–18:00 | `os-4x2mxc.objectos.app` (a staging environment) | 345 | 355 | ~60 s, hidden |

Both came from a single Chrome-on-macOS tab. The staging runtime also calls the control plane on each request (`objectos-runtime` → `/api/v1/cloud/environments/…`), so that one tab kept **both** staging containers awake around the clock. Staging container cost stayed at about $1.5/day where it should be close to zero. In the hours with no tab open (10-13 14:00–20:00), the runtime did sleep, with 0 GiB allocated.

## Proposal

Stop polling once the tab has been hidden for a while, and keep the immediate refetch when the user comes back:

- After the tab has been continuously hidden for **N minutes (suggest 10)**, the shared feeds stop arming their timer. `onVisibilityChange` already refetches immediately when the tab becomes visible again (the #4225 behaviour), so the bell is current a beat after the user looks at it.
- While hidden but under N minutes, keep today's 60 s cadence, so a tab switched away briefly still behaves exactly as now.
- Apply the same rule to any other poller that reads `document.hidden` / `visibilityState` (for example `useAiUsage`), so one stray poller cannot keep the server awake by itself.

## The trade-off (needs an explicit yes)

`useInboxArrivalNotifier` raises a **desktop notification** for new inbox messages while the tab is hidden, and its header accepts "up to about a minute late" as the cost of the 60 s hidden cadence. With this change, a message that arrives after the tab has been hidden for more than N minutes gets **no desktop notification until the user returns to the tab**. At that point it appears as the normal in-page toast or bell badge. The maintainer asked for this card knowing the trade-off. Pick N, or make it configurable, with that cost in mind.

## Done when

- A hidden tab issues no feed requests after N minutes (test: fake timers plus a `document.hidden` driver, as `sharedInboxFeed.cadence-7249.test.tsx` already does).
- Returning to the tab triggers exactly one immediate refetch per feed, then the foreground cadence.
- The `useInboxArrivalNotifier` module header and the `HIDDEN_POLL_MS` comment are updated to describe the new behaviour.

Related: #4225 (consolidated the bell's poller and kept the 60 s hidden cadence), #7249 (cadence test), #7011 (desktop notifications), cloud#2766 (staging scales to zero).
